where_to_look: The buyback program ends 2026-11-30, three days after the print. US$100m program, about US$35.5m left as of 2026-08-14 (Q2 release https://finviz.com/news/384651/x-financial-reports-second-quarter-2026-unaudited-financial-results). Check for a renewal or new program: on a ~$287m market cap (universe file) a renewal is material relative to float, and it is the most likely non-P&L line in this release.

Read-through from Chinese consumer-credit peers that reported Q3 2026 earlier in November: Qifu (QFIN), FinVolution (FINV), LexinFintech (LX), Jiayin (JFIN). Look at their loan volume, take rate, credit-cost commentary and Q4 guides under the APR-cap / lending-rule regime. Treat this as a counterparty-adjacent sector read, not a direct link.

Was the volume collapse deliberate? Q2 volume was RMB11.63bn, -70.2% YoY and -20.5% QoQ, with 91-180 DPD at 9.09% against 2.91% a year earlier (Q2 release above). Look at management's Q2 call transcript for any Q3 volume or credit direction (https://statementdog.com/analysis/XYF/earnings_calls/319514, https://www.roic.ai/quote/XYF/transcripts). Any statement in October or November (PBOC/NFRA rules on online lending, funding partner pullback) would set the bar.
Capital return cadence: the dividend is semi-annual (US$0.28/ADS declared with Q2), so the Q3 release normally carries no dividend. Check whether a special dividend or a change in payout appears.
Consensus: Nasdaq shows no EPS estimate (eps_forecast null, n_estimates N/A in the universe file), so the bar is the prior quarter's run-rate (Q2 net income RMB47.0m) and not a street number.
